items.title: Per seat or per token: read the scribe contract
items.body: Companies budgeted per seat and were billed per token, spending about two and a half times their plan. Most GP scribes are still sold per clinician, which is predictable. If a supplier moves to usage pricing, or adds agent features that run unattended, ask for a cap and monthly reporting before agreeing.

items.title: Heavy users are not the whole market
items.body: A third of large companies still report no AI use, and spending is concentrated in a few heavy users. NLW reads that as a sign of where everyone is heading; Zitron reads it as an overshoot now being reined in. For the NHS the sensible position is to pilot, measure time saved and safety, and not assume either story.

items.title: Read-only access is a useful pattern
items.body: Claude's new banking link is read-only and stops short of investment advice, deferring to regulated professionals. That is a reasonable model for clinical tools: let the system read and summarise the record, and keep the decision and the entry with a registered clinician.
